# Delivery routing ruling (e2e synthetic)

Tanya (team owner) ruled on where reaction delivery belongs:

> we route every reaction through one bundle per run per person, not one
> message per skill — a person should get one thing to read, not four

Tina pushed back on the batching window and Tanya held: the bundle closes when
the run closes, and a skill that misses the close waits for the next run rather
than sending on its own. The alternative considered and rejected was per-skill
delivery with client-side collapsing, which moves the ordering problem onto the
reader.

payload.rationale: I called perspective once and scanned the whole map: the Thematic, People, and Documents doors, plus the one ungrouped narrative. The graph is about Teamwork's anti-Slack positioning, decision capture, pricing and sprint retros; it holds nothing on reaction delivery, per-run bundling, or the batching-window dispute, and the People door is empty. I expanded the narratives and positions that frame the product problem the ruling serves (decisions evaporating in real-time chat, the anti-Slack thesis, context preservation, decision capture at consensus), plus the webhook architecture position and the Zephyr batched-delivery observation as the nearest delivery-mechanism neighbours. I deliberately did not expand the pricing, target-market, or Sprint 4 thesis-proven nodes, since they do not bear on routing. The passes should treat this document as largely new ground, with the batched-webhook observation as the closest adjacent frame.

positions.name: ReactionDeliveryBundling
positions.frame: How should reaction delivery be shaped so that a reader receives one bundle per run rather than a stream of messages per skill, and who bears the cost of ordering when the batching window closes?
positions.why: The four segments read as one directional group about where reaction delivery belongs. src-1 frames the owner's ruling, src-2 states the bundle rule (one per run per person, one thing to read), src-3 records the batching-window closing rule and the pushback that was held against, and src-4 rejects per-skill delivery with client-side collapsing because it moves ordering onto the reader. The tension is that Tina's pushback on the window was overruled, while the rule itself is reported through the memo author rather than stated first-hand. The frame keeps that tension open and does not settle it.

placements.why: No existing leaf covers how reactions reach the reader. The position's members give one directional group: one bundle per run per person, a batching window that closes with the run, and rejection of per-skill delivery that would push ordering onto the reader. This is a recurring subject about delivery shape, not a one-time fact, so it earns a leaf. It is placed under Narrative_AntiSlackPositioning as an extension, because its reduction of message noise to one readable artifact is a close, not exact, expression of the anti-Slack thesis. Narrative_DecisionCaptureAtConsensus and Narrative_DecisionsEvaporate concern capture and loss of decisions, not delivery routing, so they were weighed and not taken.
placements.title: Many per-skill messages become one bundle a reader takes in whole
placements.frame: What does a reader receive in one piece, and what has the sender left for the reader to order or collapse themselves?
